crosswalkFormat.name: RocKIT Repository Metadata Crosswalk
crosswalkFormat.description: A declarative, single-file schema inventory and reviewed mapping draft between canonical RO-Crate metadata, seven ARP profiles, seven Dataverse metadata blocks, and the complete Zenodo legacy deposition upload metadata schema. Unmatched fields remain explicitly unmapped.

canonicalModel.semanticKeyPolicy: Use a full property IRI only when it is declared by a source schema and verified as semantically portable.
canonicalModel.cardinalityPolicy: Preserve source multiplicity canonically; adapt cardinality only at repository boundaries.

placeholderPolicy.rationale: RO-Crate root identifiers and blank placeholders are not metadata values.

iriPolicy.sourceDeclaredRepositorySpecificIds: retain as provenance, not as canonical mappings
iriPolicy.unmatchedFields: record explicitly as source-only or target-only with a null mapping

provenance.dataverse: Cached Dataverse metadata blocks returned by /api/metadatablocks?returnDatasetFieldTypes=true.
provenance.caveat: The Zenodraft JSON Schema is unofficial. Official Zenodo documentation supplies required and conditional-required rules in this document.

documentModel.repositorySchema: Defines accepted fields, types, cardinalities, controlled vocabularies, and requirements.
documentModel.mapping: Connects canonical semantic properties to repository target fields.
documentModel.transformation: References a named operation in transformationLibrary; JSON never contains executable code.

omitEmpty.description: Omit null, undefined, blank strings, empty arrays, and empty objects.

omitValues.description: Omit configured placeholder values before target validation.

trim.description: Trim leading and trailing whitespace from strings.

firstNonEmpty.description: Select the first non-empty value from ordered source candidates.

first.description: Select the first item when the target is not repeatable.

asArray.description: Wrap a scalar as an array and preserve existing arrays.

normalizeDate.description: Normalize an ISO-like date to YYYY-MM-DD.

validateUrl.description: Accept only absolute URLs using configured schemes.

parseInteger.description: Convert a numeric-looking scalar to an integer.

parseNumber.description: Convert a numeric-looking scalar to a finite number.

mapVocabulary.description: Map source terms to the target controlled vocabulary.

resolveReferences.description: Resolve RO-Crate @id references against @graph before mapping.

mapEntities.description: Map resolved entities to target objects using nested field rules.
mapEntities.reversible: when every nested mapping is reversible

buildCompound.description: Construct a Dataverse compound-field object from canonical properties.
buildCompound.reversible: when every child mapping is reversible

flattenText.description: Flatten one or more text values into a single target string.

defaultValue.description: Apply a repository fallback only when no semantic source value exists.

filterByValue.description: Keep compound entities whose selected property matches a configured value.

inferResourceType.description: Infer a repository resource type from RO-Crate @type and content metadata.

deriveAccessRight.description: Derive Zenodo access_right from access conditions, embargo, and license metadata.

aggregateIdentifiers.description: Normalize identifiers and relations into a repository identifier array.

custom.description: Call a named, registered transformer for exceptional mappings.

propertyDescriptions.unitOfAnalysis: Basic unit of analysis or observation that this Dataset describes, such as individuals, families/households, groups, institutions/organizations, administrative units, and more. For information about the DDI's controlled vocabulary for this element, please refer to the DDI web page at http://www.ddialliance.org/controlled-vocabularies.
propertyDescriptions.universe: Description of the population covered by the data in the file; the group of people or other elements that are the object of the study and to which the study results refer. Age, nationality, and residence commonly help to  delineate a given universe, but any number of other factors may be used, such as age limits, sex, marital status, race, ethnic group, nationality, income, veteran status, criminal convictions, and more. The universe may consist of elements other than persons, such as housing units, court cases, deaths, countries, and so on. In general, it should be possible to tell from the description of the universe whether a given individual or element is a member of the population under study. Also known as the universe of interest, population of interest, and target population.
propertyDescriptions.timeMethod: The time method or time dimension of the data collection, such as panel, cross-sectional, trend, time- series, or other.
propertyDescriptions.dataCollector: Individual, agency or organization responsible for  administering the questionnaire or interview or compiling the data.
propertyDescriptions.collectorTraining: Type of training provided to the data collector
propertyDescriptions.frequencyOfDataCollection: If the data collected includes more than one point in time, indicate the frequency with which the data was collected; that is, monthly, quarterly, or other.
propertyDescriptions.samplingProcedure: Type of sample and sample design used to select the survey respondents to represent the population. May include reference to the target sample size and the sampling fraction.
propertyDescriptions.targetSampleSize: Specific information regarding the target sample size, actual  sample size, and the formula used to determine this.
propertyDescriptions.deviationsFromSampleDesign: Show correspondence as well as discrepancies between the sampled units (obtained) and available statistics for the population (age, sex-ratio, marital status, etc.) as a whole.
propertyDescriptions.collectionMode: Method used to collect the data; instrumentation characteristics (e.g., telephone interview, mail questionnaire, or other).
propertyDescriptions.researchInstrument: Type of data collection instrument used. Structured indicates an instrument in which all respondents are asked the same questions/tests, possibly with precoded answers. If a small portion of such a questionnaire includes open-ended questions, provide appropriate comments. Semi-structured indicates that the research instrument contains mainly open-ended questions. Unstructured indicates that in-depth interviews were conducted.
propertyDescriptions.dataCollectionSituation: Description of noteworthy aspects of the data collection situation. Includes information on factors such as cooperativeness of respondents, duration of interviews, number of call backs, or similar.
propertyDescriptions.actionsToMinimizeLoss: Summary of actions taken to minimize data loss. Include information on actions such as follow-up visits, supervisory checks, historical matching, estimation, and so on.
propertyDescriptions.controlOperations: Control OperationsMethods to facilitate data control performed by the primary investigator or by the data archive.
propertyDescriptions.weighting: The use of sampling procedures might make it necessary to apply weights to produce accurate statistical results. Describes the criteria for using weights in analysis of a collection. If a weighting formula or coefficient was developed, the formula is provided, its elements are defined, and it is indicated how the formula was applied to the data.
propertyDescriptions.cleaningOperations: Methods used to clean the data collection, such as consistency checking, wildcode checking, or other.
propertyDescriptions.datasetLevelErrorNotes: Note element used for any information annotating or clarifying the methodology and processing of the study.
propertyDescriptions.responseRate: Percentage of sample members who provided information.
propertyDescriptions.samplingErrorEstimates: Measure of how precisely one can estimate a population value from a given sample.
propertyDescriptions.otherDataAppraisal: Other issues pertaining to the data appraisal. Describe issues such as response variance, nonresponse rate  and testing for bias, interviewer and response bias, confidence levels, question bias, or similar.

universe.schema:name: universe
universe.schema:description: Description of the population covered by the data in the file; the group of people or other elements that are the object of the study and to which the study results refer. Age, nationality, and residence commonly help to  delineate a given universe, but any number of other factors may be used, such as age limits, sex, marital status, race, ethnic group, nationality, income, veteran status, criminal convictions, and more. The universe may consist of elements other than persons, such as housing units, court cases, deaths, countries, and so on. In general, it should be possible to tell from the description of the universe whether a given individual or element is a member of the population under study. Also known as the universe of interest, population of interest, and target population.
universe.hunDescription: A fájl adatai által lefedett populáció leírása; Emberek, vagy egyéb objektumok csoportja, amelyen a kutatást végzik, és amelyre az eredmény vonatkozik. Az életkor, az állampolgárság és a tartózkodási hely általában segíti az adott populáció körülhatárolását, de tetszőleges számú egyéb tényezőt is fel lehet használni, mint például korhatárok, nem, családi állapot, faj, etnikai csoport, nemzetiség, jövedelem, veterán státus, büntetőítélet és egyebek. A populácio nem csak személyekből állhat. Felépülhet lakóegységekből, bírósági ügyekből, halálesetekből, országokból és így tovább. Általánosságban a leírás alapján egy egyedről meg kell tudni mondani, hogy a vizsgált populáció tagja-e. Más néven értékelt populáció, az értékelt populáció vagy célpopuláció.
